# JusPrin Plates / Project pane implementation handoff

Implement the approved native **Plates / Project** pane in JusPrin's Prepare workspace. The Figma frames listed below are the visual source of truth; this document supplies the behavior, data ownership, integration constraints, and verification that static mockups cannot express.

The pane stays visible for simple and complex projects. The collapsed-pane exploration in frame **26g** is deliberately out of scope and must not be implemented.

## Design source

- Figma file: [JusPrin v2](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2)
- Page: **Plates & Project Pane**
- Implement the named frames below. Use their layers, variables, existing component instances, dimensions, spacing, states, and copy directly from Figma instead of recreating the visuals from prose.

| Figma frame | Implementation state |
| --- | --- |
| `26a · Ordinary two-plate job · Plates` | Default two-plate state |
| `26b · Complex plate · Plates` | Copies, materials, modifier/negative part, disabled copy, mesh errors, and Not on a plate |
| `26c1 · One plate, one object` | Minimum-content state; the pane still remains visible |
| `26c2 · Folded plate summaries` | Computed summaries for inactive folded plates |
| `26d1 · Plate row menu` | Plate overflow menu |
| `26d2 · Object row menu` | Object overflow menu |
| `26e1 · Project with metadata` | Project root with 3MF metadata |
| `26e2 · Project details` | Full metadata and attachment entry points |
| `26e3 · Project print history` | Detailed physical-print records plus a count-only older record |
| `26e4 · Count-only print history` | Projects whose older prints have only a count |
| `26f · Project without metadata` | Honest no-metadata state |
| `26h · Customization mark comparison` | Decision record; implement the recommended `h2` single-mark treatment |

Do not implement `26g`, a collapse rail, a collapse control, or any persistence for a collapsed state. Do not restore the old 25-series pane mockups.

## Product boundary

Build this as a fork-owned native wxWidgets surface under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. OrcaSlicer's project model, plate list, selection, slicing results, undo history, context actions, project metadata, and serialization remain authoritative.

The pane presents and invokes those owners. It must not create a second project model, infer project facts from labels or canvas coordinates, simulate clicks against hidden controls, or add a separate undo path.

Keep these controls in their current homes:

- model import;
- printer, nozzle, and material setup;
- Slice and Print;
- move, rotate, scale, and other spatial tools;
- the Agent conversation.

Do not add permanent action rows for operations that belong in the plate or object overflow menu.

## Plates tab behavior

### Plate and selection state

- Show every plate, including a one-plate project.
- Keep the active plate expanded. Keep all other plates folded.
- Selecting a plate row activates the same Orca plate in the 3D view.
- Selecting an object, copy, part, modifier, negative part, or support volume selects that exact Orca item when Orca supports that selection granularity.
- Reflect selection changes made in the 3D view back into the pane without delay or stale highlights.
- Switching between Plates and Project must not change the active plate or canvas selection.
- Clear project-scoped IDs and pane expansion state when `project_session` changes.

### Plate rows and folded summaries

- Derive **Sliced** versus **Needs slice** from the current authoritative slice state.
- A folded plate summary is computed from current plate membership. It is not editable text and is not stored separately.
- If a plate contains one distinct object, show its name and total copy count when greater than one.
- If a plate contains several distinct objects, show the object count used by Figma.
- Include disabled copies in the total. Append the separate **N won't print** phrase when applicable.
- Show lock or customized-plate-settings indicators only when those facts apply.
- **Add plate** must call Orca's existing plate creation path and participate in Orca undo/redo.

### Object rows and hierarchy

- Show the object name and copy count.
- Show filament/color assignment only for a multi-material job or an object-specific override.
- Make a disabled object's or copy's **won't print** state explicit.
- Show **Not on a plate** only when at least one object instance belongs to no plate. Membership comes from `PartPlateList`, not bounding-box guesses made by the pane.
- A simple object remains one row.
- Add disclosure children only for data that exists: copies, model parts, modifiers, negative parts, support enforcers, or support blockers.
- Do not introduce a permanent synthetic assembly level.
- Keep intentional customization separate from mesh problems. Implement the recommended `h2` treatment in frame 26h: one gray customization mark opens the list of applicable Orca tools/settings. Mesh problems use the distinct error treatment in Figma.

### Context menus

Use the menu contents and ordering from frames 26d1 and 26d2. Route every command to Orca's existing behavior rather than reimplementing it in the pane.

Plate menu:

- Rename
- Arrange
- Auto-orient
- Lock or Unlock
- Plate settings
- Delete plate
- Show Move to front and filament grouping only when their existing Orca preconditions apply.

Object menu:

- Use Orca's existing object context actions for quantity, printability, filament, per-object settings, repair, split, rename, and delete.
- A copy row exposes the same relevant menu path for that copy.
- Right-clicking a row and clicking its overflow button must open the same menu model.

## Project tab behavior

### Identity and metadata

- The saved JusPrin project name and save state come from managed project persistence. They are not the model title stored in the 3MF.
- The model title, designer/author, license, description, profile metadata, cover images, and packed files come from Orca's project metadata and `Workspace::ProjectDetails`.
- Never synthesize a model title from the project name or source filename.
- Omit missing metadata. Do not render blank fields or placeholders.
- When no model metadata exists, use frame 26f exactly and keep **Edit Project Info** available.
- **Details** opens the nested pane view in frame 26e2. Show only sections backed by data.
- Attachment categories should map to Orca's existing packed-file categories. Bill of materials, assembly guide, images, and other files remain Orca project attachments; do not copy them into a second store.
- **Edit Project Info** opens Orca's existing project-information editor.

### Project root actions

- **Printed N times** opens print history.
- **Details** opens project details.
- **Version history** opens the existing managed autosave history and preserves its current restore confirmation, pinning, validation, and failure behavior.
- **Export project 3MF…** opens the existing system save dialog and uses `ProjectAutosave::export_copy`. It is separate from exporting G-code or a sliced 3MF.
- Moving these entry points from `StatusRow` must preserve current functionality and error handling. Recent projects and Preferences may remain in the header overflow menu.

### Nested navigation

- A Project subview uses the back action shown in Figma to return to the Project root.
- Escape goes up one Project level when a subview is open.
- Escape at the Project root does not switch to Plates.
- Clicking the Plates tab always returns directly to the plate list while preserving plate and object selection.
- A new project starts on the Project root. Do not show a subview retained from the previous project.

## Print history truthfulness

`Agent::ProjectStateDocument::physical_prints()` is the authoritative physical-print ledger. Do not construct history from slice events, exports, or UI activity.

- The root count comes from `physical_print_count()`.
- A detailed row may show only fields present in its `PhysicalPrintRecord`: timestamps, plate, printer, outcome, and related recorded facts.
- Duration may be derived only when both recorded timestamps are valid.
- Material weight, cost, and predicted time in `SliceStatistics` are slice/build estimates. Label them as estimates as shown in frame 26e3; never present them as measured physical consumption or duration.
- Do not add a currency symbol unless the persisted record identifies the currency. A bare stored cost is not enough to guess dollars.
- Omit any missing field instead of substituting zero or placeholder copy.
- Preserve count-only history for migrated/older data. Use frame 26e4 when no detailed records exist, and the count-only row from 26e3 when detailed and legacy records coexist.
- Map outcomes to localized user-facing labels without losing the persisted distinction among `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`.
- Subscribe to ledger changes without taking away the listener needed by another shell component. If the existing single-listener persistence API cannot support both `StatusRow` and the pane during migration, replace it with safe multi-subscriber ownership before moving the count.

## Current code map and known gaps

Start with the canonical documents in `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`. Before changing an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.

Likely integration points:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp` and `.hpp`: place the fork-owned pane as the left sibling of the existing workspace. Keep the stock Notebook pages and Agent-pane lifecycle intact.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp`: extend the fork-owned projection with the smallest behavior-oriented data and commands the pane needs.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`: read current plate membership, slice state, selection, object hierarchy, metadata, and customization facts; delegate mutations to their Orca owners.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp`: refresh on Selection, Objects, Plates, Project, Settings, History, Transform, undo/redo, slicing, and project replacement as relevant.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`: migrate Project entry points and print count after the pane owns them, without changing Recent projects, Preferences, or unrelated header behavior.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.hpp`: read physical-print records and counts.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CanvasPresentationController.cpp`: keep the legacy Orca sidebar and plate overlays hidden; the new pane supplies visible navigation.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.cpp`: preserve the existing object tools and right-click path.

The current workspace snapshot is not sufficient for every approved row. Confirm and close these gaps before building presentation code around assumptions:

1. `WorkspacePlate::objects` does not expose per-instance IDs, per-instance printability, or off-plate instances.
2. `ObjectDetails` exposes counts but not the named child rows needed for parts, modifiers, negative parts, or support volumes.
3. Plate selection and all row-menu commands do not yet share one public UI command surface.
4. Intentional customization needs explicit facts for support painting, color painting, variable layer height, per-object overrides, and plate settings.
5. Mesh repair/problem status needs a stable read model separate from customization state.
6. Project metadata exposes attachment identifiers and categories; the pane still needs the existing Orca paths that open each detail or attachment.

Expose the smallest strict API that represents each missing fact or command. Keep preconditions in the caller that owns the workflow and let unexpected failures remain visible.

## Design-system and component rules

Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before writing UI code.

- Every color, radius, font, and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` through `ShellTheme` or `ShellRecipes`.
- Layout gaps use the documented spacing scale.
- If a required value has no token, add the token and its guard before using it.
- Reuse established generic primitives such as icons, icon buttons, tabs, menus, swatches, typography, and selection treatments.
- Keep feature-specific plate rows, object rows, metadata blocks, and history records as pane-owned composition unless another production surface already has the same reusable contract.
- Do not add Figma-style specimen components or one-off variants to the production design system merely because several mockup frames repeat a structure.
- Support light and dark themes, keyboard focus, localization, and 100%, 150%, and 200% display scaling.

## Suggested implementation order

1. Add tests for the missing read model: plate membership, per-copy printability, folded summaries, off-plate instances, hierarchy counts/children, customization facts, and mesh-problem status.
2. Add the smallest workspace commands for plate selection/addition and menu actions that do not already have a fork-owned seam.
3. Build the pane shell and tab/navigation state using frame 26c1 first.
4. Add the ordinary and folded multi-plate states from 26a and 26c2.
5. Add complex object hierarchy and conditional indicators from 26b and 26h.
6. Route the menus from 26d1 and 26d2 to existing Orca actions.
7. Add the Project root and metadata states from 26e1, 26e2, and 26f.
8. Move version history/export/details/count entry points from `StatusRow` only after their pane replacements pass end-to-end tests.
9. Add print history from the persisted ledger using 26e3 and 26e4.
10. Run visual and behavioral verification across supported platforms and scaling levels.

## Acceptance criteria

### Behavior

- One plate and one object still show the pane and both tabs.
- Plate selection, object selection, canvas selection, active plate, and row highlights stay synchronized in both directions.
- Folded summaries remain correct after add, delete, duplicate, disable, move between plates, arrange, undo/redo, project restore, and project replacement.
- Simple objects stay simple. Child rows appear only for existing copies, parts, modifiers, negative parts, and support volumes.
- Not on a plate appears only with real off-plate content.
- Every plate and object menu action reaches the existing Orca behavior and undo history.
- Project name and 3MF model title never substitute for one another.
- Missing metadata uses 26f without invented or blank values.
- Version restore and project export preserve existing confirmations, validation, and failure behavior.
- Print history displays only persisted facts and clearly labeled estimates.
- Frame 26g behavior is absent.

### Visual and accessibility

- Compare every implemented state against its named Figma frame.
- Verify light and dark themes at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Verify keyboard traversal, visible focus, menu invocation, Escape behavior, screen-reader labels, truncation, long localized text, and narrow-window behavior.
- Status is never conveyed by color alone.

### Regression coverage

- Run `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, and the existing AgentUI tests required by the design-system guide.
- Add focused native tests for the pane read model and commands.
- Exercise the local multi-plate workflow end to end, including project metadata, physical-print history, version history, and export.
- Use the fake-printer workflow in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` when printer-connected behavior is involved. Use an isolated `--datadir` and never drive another JusPrin instance.
- If an OrcaSlicer-owned file changes, include the rebase evidence required by `fork-stewardship.md`.

This is a temporary implementation handoff. Keep it untracked until Kenneth decides it is ready to commit.

9	- Figma file: [JusPrin v2](https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2)
10	- Page: **Plates & Project Pane**
11	- Implement the named frames below. Use their layers, variables, existing component instances, dimensions, spacing, states, and copy directly from Figma instead of recreating the visuals from prose.
12	
13	| Figma frame | Implementation state |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| `26a · Ordinary two-plate job · Plates` | Default two-plate state |
16	| `26b · Complex plate · Plates` | Copies, materials, modifier/negative part, disabled copy, mesh errors, and Not on a plate |
17	| `26c1 · One plate, one object` | Minimum-content state; the pane still remains visible |
18	| `26c2 · Folded plate summaries` | Computed summaries for inactive folded plates |
19	| `26d1 · Plate row menu` | Plate overflow menu |
20	| `26d2 · Object row menu` | Object overflow menu |
21	| `26e1 · Project with metadata` | Project root with 3MF metadata |
22	| `26e2 · Project details` | Full metadata and attachment entry points |
23	| `26e3 · Project print history` | Detailed physical-print records plus a count-only older record |
24	| `26e4 · Count-only print history` | Projects whose older prints have only a count |
25	| `26f · Project without metadata` | Honest no-metadata state |
26	| `26h · Customization mark comparison` | Decision record; implement the recommended `h2` single-mark treatment |
27	
28	Do not implement `26g`, a collapse rail, a collapse control, or any persistence for a collapsed state. Do not restore the old 25-series pane mockups.
29	
30	## Product boundary
31	
32	Build this as a fork-owned native wxWidgets surface under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. OrcaSlicer's project model, plate list, selection, slicing results, undo history, context actions, project metadata, and serialization remain authoritative.
33	
34	The pane presents and invokes those owners. It must not create a second project model, infer project facts from labels or canvas coordinates, simulate clicks against hidden controls, or add a separate undo path.
35	
36	Keep these controls in their current homes:
37	
38	- model import;
39	- printer, nozzle, and material setup;
40	- Slice and Print;
41	- move, rotate, scale, and other spatial tools;
42	- the Agent conversation.
43	
44	Do not add permanent action rows for operations that belong in the plate or object overflow menu.
45	
46	## Plates tab behavior
47	
48	### Plate and selection state
49	
50	- Show every plate, including a one-plate project.
51	- Keep the active plate expanded. Keep all other plates folded.
52	- Selecting a plate row activates the same Orca plate in the 3D view.
53	- Selecting an object, copy, part, modifier, negative part, or support volume selects that exact Orca item when Orca supports that selection granularity.
54	- Reflect selection changes made in the 3D view back into the pane without delay or stale highlights.
55	- Switching between Plates and Project must not change the active plate or canvas selection.
56	- Clear project-scoped IDs and pane expansion state when `project_session` changes.
57	
58	### Plate rows and folded summaries
59	
60	- Derive **Sliced** versus **Needs slice** from the current authoritative slice state.
61	- A folded plate summary is computed from current plate membership. It is not editable text and is not stored separately.
62	- If a plate contains one distinct object, show its name and total copy count when greater than one.
63	- If a plate contains several distinct objects, show the object count used by Figma.
64	- Include disabled copies in the total. Append the separate **N won't print** phrase when applicable.
65	- Show lock or customized-plate-settings indicators only when those facts apply.
66	- **Add plate** must call Orca's existing plate creation path and participate in Orca undo/redo.
67	
68	### Object rows and hierarchy
69	
70	- Show the object name and copy count.
71	- Show filament/color assignment only for a multi-material job or an object-specific override.
72	- Make a disabled object's or copy's **won't print** state explicit.
73	- Show **Not on a plate** only when at least one object instance belongs to no plate. Membership comes from `PartPlateList`, not bounding-box guesses made by the pane.
74	- A simple object remains one row.
75	- Add disclosure children only for data that exists: copies, model parts, modifiers, negative parts, support enforcers, or support blockers.
76	- Do not introduce a permanent synthetic assembly level.
77	- Keep intentional customization separate from mesh problems. Implement the recommended `h2` treatment in frame 26h: one gray customization mark opens the list of applicable Orca tools/settings. Mesh problems use the distinct error treatment in Figma.
78	
79	### Context menus
80	
81	Use the menu contents and ordering from frames 26d1 and 26d2. Route every command to Orca's existing behavior rather than reimplementing it in the pane.
82	
83	Plate menu:
84	
85	- Rename
86	- Arrange
87	- Auto-orient
88	- Lock or Unlock
89	- Plate settings
90	- Delete plate
91	- Show Move to front and filament grouping only when their existing Orca preconditions apply.
92	
93	Object menu:
94	
95	- Use Orca's existing object context actions for quantity, printability, filament, per-object settings, repair, split, rename, and delete.
96	- A copy row exposes the same relevant menu path for that copy.
97	- Right-clicking a row and clicking its overflow button must open the same menu model.
98	
99	## Project tab behavior
100	
101	### Identity and metadata
102	
103	- The saved JusPrin project name and save state come from managed project persistence. They are not the model title stored in the 3MF.
104	- The model title, designer/author, license, description, profile metadata, cover images, and packed files come from Orca's project metadata and `Workspace::ProjectDetails`.
105	- Never synthesize a model title from the project name or source filename.
106	- Omit missing metadata. Do not render blank fields or placeholders.
107	- When no model metadata exists, use frame 26f exactly and keep **Edit Project Info** available.
108	- **Details** opens the nested pane view in frame 26e2. Show only sections backed by data.
109	- Attachment categories should map to Orca's existing packed-file categories. Bill of materials, assembly guide, images, and other files remain Orca project attachments; do not copy them into a second store.
110	- **Edit Project Info** opens Orca's existing project-information editor.
111	
112	### Project root actions
113	
114	- **Printed N times** opens print history.
115	- **Details** opens project details.
116	- **Version history** opens the existing managed autosave history and preserves its current restore confirmation, pinning, validation, and failure behavior.
117	- **Export project 3MF…** opens the existing system save dialog and uses `ProjectAutosave::export_copy`. It is separate from exporting G-code or a sliced 3MF.
118	- Moving these entry points from `StatusRow` must preserve current functionality and error handling. Recent projects and Preferences may remain in the header overflow menu.
119	
120	### Nested navigation
121	
122	- A Project subview uses the back action shown in Figma to return to the Project root.
123	- Escape goes up one Project level when a subview is open.
124	- Escape at the Project root does not switch to Plates.
125	- Clicking the Plates tab always returns directly to the plate list while preserving plate and object selection.
126	- A new project starts on the Project root. Do not show a subview retained from the previous project.
127	
128	## Print history truthfulness
129	
130	`Agent::ProjectStateDocument::physical_prints()` is the authoritative physical-print ledger. Do not construct history from slice events, exports, or UI activity.
131	
132	- The root count comes from `physical_print_count()`.
133	- A detailed row may show only fields present in its `PhysicalPrintRecord`: timestamps, plate, printer, outcome, and related recorded facts.
134	- Duration may be derived only when both recorded timestamps are valid.
135	- Material weight, cost, and predicted time in `SliceStatistics` are slice/build estimates. Label them as estimates as shown in frame 26e3; never present them as measured physical consumption or duration.
136	- Do not add a currency symbol unless the persisted record identifies the currency. A bare stored cost is not enough to guess dollars.
137	- Omit any missing field instead of substituting zero or placeholder copy.
138	- Preserve count-only history for migrated/older data. Use frame 26e4 when no detailed records exist, and the count-only row from 26e3 when detailed and legacy records coexist.
139	- Map outcomes to localized user-facing labels without losing the persisted distinction among `completed`, `failed`, and `cancelled`.
140	- Subscribe to ledger changes without taking away the listener needed by another shell component. If the existing single-listener persistence API cannot support both `StatusRow` and the pane during migration, replace it with safe multi-subscriber ownership before moving the count.
141	
142	## Current code map and known gaps
143	
144	Start with the canonical documents in `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`. Before changing an OrcaSlicer-owned file, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`.
145	
146	Likely integration points:
147	
148	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp` and `.hpp`: place the fork-owned pane as the left sibling of the existing workspace. Keep the stock Notebook pages and Agent-pane lifecycle intact.
149	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp`: extend the fork-owned projection with the smallest behavior-oriented data and commands the pane needs.
150	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`: read current plate membership, slice state, selection, object hierarchy, metadata, and customization facts; delegate mutations to their Orca owners.
151	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp`: refresh on Selection, Objects, Plates, Project, Settings, History, Transform, undo/redo, slicing, and project replacement as relevant.
152	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`: migrate Project entry points and print count after the pane owns them, without changing Recent projects, Preferences, or unrelated header behavior.
153	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.hpp`: read physical-print records and counts.
154	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CanvasPresentationController.cpp`: keep the legacy Orca sidebar and plate overlays hidden; the new pane supplies visible navigation.
155	- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStrip.cpp`: preserve the existing object tools and right-click path.
156	
157	The current workspace snapshot is not sufficient for every approved row. Confirm and close these gaps before building presentation code around assumptions:
158	
159	1. `WorkspacePlate::objects` does not expose per-instance IDs, per-instance printability, or off-plate instances.
160	2. `ObjectDetails` exposes counts but not the named child rows needed for parts, modifiers, negative parts, or support volumes.
161	3. Plate selection and all row-menu commands do not yet share one public UI command surface.
162	4. Intentional customization needs explicit facts for support painting, color painting, variable layer height, per-object overrides, and plate settings.
163	5. Mesh repair/problem status needs a stable read model separate from customization state.
164	6. Project metadata exposes attachment identifiers and categories; the pane still needs the existing Orca paths that open each detail or attachment.
165	
166	Expose the smallest strict API that represents each missing fact or command. Keep preconditions in the caller that owns the workflow and let unexpected failures remain visible.
167	
168	## Design-system and component rules
169	
170	Follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before writing UI code.
171	
172	- Every color, radius, font, and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` through `ShellTheme` or `ShellRecipes`.
173	- Layout gaps use the documented spacing scale.
174	- If a required value has no token, add the token and its guard before using it.
175	- Reuse established generic primitives such as icons, icon buttons, tabs, menus, swatches, typography, and selection treatments.
176	- Keep feature-specific plate rows, object rows, metadata blocks, and history records as pane-owned composition unless another production surface already has the same reusable contract.
177	- Do not add Figma-style specimen components or one-off variants to the production design system merely because several mockup frames repeat a structure.
178	- Support light and dark themes, keyboard focus, localization, and 100%, 150%, and 200% display scaling.
179	
180	## Suggested implementation order
181	
182	1. Add tests for the missing read model: plate membership, per-copy printability, folded summaries, off-plate instances, hierarchy counts/children, customization facts, and mesh-problem status.
183	2. Add the smallest workspace commands for plate selection/addition and menu actions that do not already have a fork-owned seam.
184	3. Build the pane shell and tab/navigation state using frame 26c1 first.
185	4. Add the ordinary and folded multi-plate states from 26a and 26c2.
186	5. Add complex object hierarchy and conditional indicators from 26b and 26h.
187	6. Route the menus from 26d1 and 26d2 to existing Orca actions.
188	7. Add the Project root and metadata states from 26e1, 26e2, and 26f.
189	8. Move version history/export/details/count entry points from `StatusRow` only after their pane replacements pass end-to-end tests.
190	9. Add print history from the persisted ledger using 26e3 and 26e4.
191	10. Run visual and behavioral verification across supported platforms and scaling levels.
192	
193	## Acceptance criteria
194	
195	### Behavior
196	
197	- One plate and one object still show the pane and both tabs.
198	- Plate selection, object selection, canvas selection, active plate, and row highlights stay synchronized in both directions.
199	- Folded summaries remain correct after add, delete, duplicate, disable, move between plates, arrange, undo/redo, project restore, and project replacement.
200	- Simple objects stay simple. Child rows appear only for existing copies, parts, modifiers, negative parts, and support volumes.
201	- Not on a plate appears only with real off-plate content.
202	- Every plate and object menu action reaches the existing Orca behavior and undo history.
203	- Project name and 3MF model title never substitute for one another.
204	- Missing metadata uses 26f without invented or blank values.
205	- Version restore and project export preserve existing confirmations, validation, and failure behavior.
206	- Print history displays only persisted facts and clearly labeled estimates.
207	- Frame 26g behavior is absent.
208	
209	### Visual and accessibility
210	
211	- Compare every implemented state against its named Figma frame.
212	- Verify light and dark themes at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
213	- Verify keyboard traversal, visible focus, menu invocation, Escape behavior, screen-reader labels, truncation, long localized text, and narrow-window behavior.
214	- Status is never conveyed by color alone.
215	
216	### Regression coverage
217	
218	- Run `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, and the existing AgentUI tests required by the design-system guide.
219	- Add focused native tests for the pane read model and commands.
220	- Exercise the local multi-plate workflow end to end, including project metadata, physical-print history, version history, and export.
221	- Use the fake-printer workflow in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` when printer-connected behavior is involved. Use an isolated `--datadir` and never drive another JusPrin instance.
222	- If an OrcaSlicer-owned file changes, include the rebase evidence required by `fork-stewardship.md`.
223	
224	This is a temporary implementation handoff. Keep it untracked until Kenneth decides it is ready to commit.
225	
</system-reminder>

1	# JusPrin engineering and verification method
2	
3	**Status:** Required planning, implementation, and release-verification method for `jusprin-newui`.
4	
5	JusPrin is changing the presentation of a mature manufacturing application. The main engineering risk is not whether common UI technology can work; it is whether new presentation code bypasses, duplicates, or destabilizes authoritative Orca behavior.
6	
7	## Risk vocabulary
8	
9	Risk means residual, evidence-backed uncertainty that could materially affect architecture, correctness, delivery, regressions, or a physical print after mature precedent has been considered.
10	
11	Keep these categories separate:
12	
13	- **Feasibility:** whether a technical boundary can work at all.
14	- **Integration:** whether proven components can be connected without unsafe ownership or duplicated behavior.
15	- **Product behavior:** uncertainty about what the feature must do.
16	- **Delivery effort:** understood implementation work, even when substantial.
17	- **Regression exposure:** risk of disturbing mature Orca behavior.
18	- **Platform QA:** evidence required for a particular OS, WebView backend, display stack, input method, or DPI.
19	
20	A known bug, untested platform, or inconvenient implementation detail is not automatically an architecture risk.
21	
22	## Required assessment process
23	
24	Before adding a spike or assigning a risk label:
25	
26	1. Define the user-visible requirement without assuming an implementation or cause.
27	2. Classify the underlying technical capability.
28	3. Search for mature precedent in the current Orca code, Orca history and forks, comparable slicers, mature same-stack applications, and finally framework documentation.
29	4. State what the precedent proves and where it differs.
30	5. Isolate only the unproven delta.
31	6. Record the plausible failure, evidence for likelihood, consequence, blast radius, reversibility, and cheapest resolving evidence.
32	7. Choose code inspection, a focused test, an integration prototype, platform validation, or a feasibility spike according to the uncertainty.
33	
34	A new visual arrangement is not necessarily a new technical capability. Spike only consequential uncertainty that mature code and focused tests cannot answer.
35	
36	## Current evidence ledger
37	
38	| Requirement | Established evidence | Remaining production delta | Current classification |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| Native shell | Orca already composes native panels and `GLCanvas3D`; the exact native/WebView boundary ran on macOS and Linux/X11 | Production shell behavior and remaining platform/input coverage | Very low feasibility; integration and platform QA remain |
41	| Agent pane and bridge | Orca has local/remote WebViews, script handlers, and native/JS communication | Versioned schema, recovery, focus rules, authentication, production UI | Low architecture risk |
42	| Thin object/plate pane | `GUI_ObjectList`, `ObjectDataViewModel`, `Plater`, and `PartPlate` contain the behavior | A small behavior-oriented API without copied presentation logic | Low feasibility; medium integration |
43	| Canvas action strip | Orca projects selection bounds and activates gizmos | Product positioning rules and reusable controller | Low |
44	| Exact transform entry | `GizmoObjectManipulation` applies values and snapshots | Separate behavior from old ImGui presentation | Low feasibility; medium coupling |
45	| Semantic facet annotations | Existing painter tools prove picking, painting, visualization, copying, undo, and persistence | Arbitrary label schema and lifecycle, especially topology changes | Low feasibility; medium data-model risk |
46	| Gizmo rollout | Existing tools share selection, rendering, and history infrastructure | Different interaction families need distinct adapters | Medium delivery/regression; low architecture |
47	| Slicing, picking, history, Preview | Mature production subsystems retained unchanged | Ensure presentation never bypasses them | Low when boundary is enforced |
48	
49	Update this ledger when evidence changes. Do not carry an old risk label forward without checking current code and results.
50	
51	## Test strategy
52	
53	### Regression baselines and failure classification
54	
55	Run the closest existing test and the broadest practical baseline before changing
56	an upstream-owned behavior. Record pre-existing failures by exact test name and
57	failure mode so later runs can distinguish a regression from inherited state.
58	
59	When a broad suite fails, rerun the exact case independently before assigning a
60	cause. Record repeatable failures as regressions until disproved; record a
61	one-time timeout, deadlock, or infrastructure failure separately with the
62	isolated rerun result. A green focused suite does not erase a new repeatable
63	broad-suite failure.
64	
65	### Contract tests
66	
67	Test strong IDs, invalid/missing/stale identifiers, command errors, subscription lifetime, event coalescing, revision behavior, and fake-workspace history without linking the GUI. Test both successful and unsuccessful commands, and assert that reported results agree with authoritative state.
68	
69	### Real-adapter application tests
70	
71	A fake cannot validate `Plater`, `GLCanvas3D`, plate membership, `GUI_ObjectList` dependencies, event ordering, or Orca's undo stack. Add an application-level harness that loads deterministic project fixtures and covers:
72	
73	- project-ready signaling rather than fixed event-loop delays;
74	- a dedicated application name and bundle identity so UI automation cannot target another Orca build;
75	- an isolated temporary configuration and repository-owned fixture;
76	- deterministic on-bed object placement, active tab, selection, and camera-visible state before reporting readiness;
77	- object and viewport selection in both directions;
78	- rename, duplicate, remove, plate switch, import, undo, and redo;
79	- committed native transform and exact-value transform;
80	- callback snapshots at the advertised revision;
81	- subscriber destruction;
82	- project replacement and session-ID invalidation;
83	- operations initiated outside the adapter.
84	
85	The POC self-test is evidence and test-design input, not a production harness: its STL setup could not reproduce rename undo, and it intentionally terminated through `std::_Exit`.
86	
87	### Shell end-to-end tests
88	
89	Run the complete native application with a deterministic multi-plate project. Verify the visible real canvas, camera controls, selection, native gizmos, Slice, Check print, return to Prepare, undo/redo, object pane synchronization, Agent pane persistence, resize, maximize/restore, and the unchanged legacy layout when testing a compatibility mode.
90	
91	Visual appearance alone is insufficient. Validate state from authoritative callbacks and pair visibility claims with screenshots or rendered evidence.
92	
93	Use the harness to establish deterministic application state; use UI automation
94	for real pointer, keyboard, focus, and rendering checks rather than for fragile
95	startup setup. For canvas policy, inventory every overlay surface and verify
96	rendering and hit-testing separately. Compare a stock window with the product
97	policy, then exercise selection, orbit, pan, zoom, active gizmo input, slicing,
98	Preview, and restoration of the prior presentation state.
99	
100	### Printer tests without hardware
101	
102	Bambu paths (printer-menu Idle / Printing / Offline, Select Machine, print job)
103	are exercised by an in-process fake that substitutes for the Bambu printer
104	agent while a real Bambu Lab **system** preset stays selected. How to turn it
105	on, the JSON control file, isolated-instance rules for agents, and acceptance
106	checks: [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md).
107	
108	The Klipper/Moonraker network simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`
109	under `tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host paths. Do not add a fake
110	Bambu network layer (MQTT/FTPS/discovery) without an explicit request.
111	
112	### Platform matrix
113	
114	Before release completion, cover:
115	
116	- Windows with WebView2;
117	- macOS with WKWebView;
118	- Linux/X11 and supported Wayland configurations with WebKitGTK;
119	- supported CPU architectures and a physical GPU where applicable;
120	- 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling or equivalent platform DPI settings;
121	- light and dark mode;
122	- keyboard focus, global shortcuts, clipboard, text selection, and IME composition;
123	- WebView startup, local resource loading, reload, and recovery;
124	- streaming scroll anchoring while orbiting and resizing;
125	- idle and streaming CPU/memory observations.
126	
127	Classify localized CSS, focus, packaging, or backend problems as platform defects unless evidence shows they require a different architecture.
128	
129	### Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU
130	
131	A Windows machine with no graphics driver reports system GL 1.1, so the launcher
132	(`src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp`) loads `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` instead.
133	Nothing in CMake or this repository supplies that file or what it depends on, so
134	provision every freshly configured build tree with
135	`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1`.
136	Placement is not interchangeable:
137	
138	| file | goes | because |
139	| --- | --- | --- |
140	| `opengl32.dll` | `mesa\` subfolder | the launcher loads it by that path; beside the executable it shadows the system GL and the app dies at launch |
141	| `opengl32.dll` again | beside each `*_harness.exe` | a harness links the app in and has no launcher, so only a copy beside it replaces the system GL 1.1 |
142	| `libgallium_wgl.dll` | beside the executable | the `opengl32.dll` stub imports it, and Windows resolves imports against the process directory |
143	| `dxil.dll` | beside the executable | Mesa's `d3d12` driver signs translated shaders with it; Windows Server does not ship it, Windows SDKs carry it under `Redist\D3D\x64` |
144	
145	Each gap has its own silent signature:
146	
147	- **No `libgallium_wgl.dll`:** GL falls back to 1.1, the log has `glcontext not ready, postpone init` and no `got opengl version` line, and the canvas stays black for the whole session — the retry after a postponed init exists only on Linux.
148	- **No `opengl32.dll` beside a harness:** the same GL 1.1 signature, in the harness only. The canvas never builds its volumes, so `Plater::select_object` returns false after `load_files`, and the workspace harness then crashed opening a paint gizmo with nothing selected (`0xC0000005`).
149	- **No `dxil.dll`:** GL initializes through `d3d12`, then the process exits with `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw, with no log line, no dialog, and no event-log entry. `slow_bootup` only moves this crash from startup to the first canvas paint.
150	
151	Confirm what actually loaded from the process's module list rather than from
152	file presence. The log names the live driver: `4.6 … llvmpipe` is Mesa's software
153	rasterizer, `4.2 … D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` is Mesa's `d3d12`
154	driver on WARP. A fully provisioned tree renders under both;
155	`GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` selects the former.
156	
157	## Implementation evidence record
158	
159	For every production area, record:
160	
161	- product requirement and underlying technical nature;
162	- current Orca command owner, snapshot location, and event source;
163	- mature precedents and what each proves;
164	- remaining delta and risk category;
165	- production and upstream-owned files touched;
166	- verification command and exit condition;
167	- platforms exercised and gaps remaining;
168	- regression checks for the original Orca path;
169	- any behavior that could not be tested and why.
170	
171	## Rebase evidence
172	
173	The rules for changing upstream-owned files are in [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). This section states only what a change must produce as evidence.
174	
175	A change that touches an upstream-owned file is not finished until the handback or pull request records three things:
176	
177	1. **The rebase simulation and its result**, run against current upstream with both endpoint commits named. For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy resolution is a defect to fix before the change lands, not a note for the person who rebases.
178	2. **Every upstream line deleted or rewritten**, with where the logic went and why an additive form was not possible.
179	3. **What the fork now owns** — product policy, a small neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.
180	
181	An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It never proves that a future rebase will merge, and never proves that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the contract tests, the full native build, the multi-plate Prepare/Check workflow, native gizmo input, and the original-Orca regression checks.
182	
183	The incidents that produced these rules are in [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md). Historical logs and spike procedures are in [POC reference](poc-reference.md).
184

| `opengl32.dll` again | beside each `*_harness.exe` | a harness links the app in and has no launcher, so only a copy beside it replaces the system GL 1.1 |
| `libgallium_wgl.dll` | beside the executable | the `opengl32.dll` stub imports it, and Windows resolves imports against the process directory |
| `dxil.dll` | beside the executable | Mesa's `d3d12` driver signs translated shaders with it; Windows Server does not ship it, Windows SDKs carry it under `Redist\D3D\x64` |

Each gap has its own silent signature:

- **No `libgallium_wgl.dll`:** GL falls back to 1.1, the log has `glcontext not ready, postpone init` and no `got opengl version` line, and the canvas stays black for the whole session — the retry after a postponed init exists only on Linux.
- **No `opengl32.dll` beside a harness:** the same GL 1.1 signature, in the harness only. The canvas never builds its volumes, so `Plater::select_object` returns false after `load_files`, and the workspace harness then crashed opening a paint gizmo with nothing selected (`0xC0000005`).
- **No `dxil.dll`:** GL initializes through `d3d12`, then the process exits with `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw, with no log line, no dialog, and no event-log entry. `slow_bootup` only moves this crash from startup to the first canvas paint.

Confirm what actually loaded from the process's module list rather than from
file presence. The log names the live driver: `4.6 … llvmpipe` is Mesa's software
rasterizer, `4.2 … D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` is Mesa's `d3d12`
driver on WARP. A fully provisioned tree renders under both;
`GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` selects the former.

## Implementation evidence record

For every production area, record:

- product requirement and underlying technical nature;
- current Orca command owner, snapshot location, and event source;
- mature precedents and what each proves;
- remaining delta and risk category;
- production and upstream-owned files touched;
- verification command and exit condition;
- platforms exercised and gaps remaining;
- regression checks for the original Orca path;
- any behavior that could not be tested and why.

## Rebase evidence

The rules for changing upstream-owned files are in [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). This section states only what a change must produce as evidence.

A change that touches an upstream-owned file is not finished until the handback or pull request records three things:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result**, run against current upstream with both endpoint commits named. For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy resolution is a defect to fix before the change lands, not a note for the person who rebases.
2. **Every upstream line deleted or rewritten**, with where the logic went and why an additive form was not possible.
3. **What the fork now owns** — product policy, a small neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It never proves that a future rebase will merge, and never proves that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the contract tests, the full native build, the multi-plate Prepare/Check workflow, native gizmo input, and the original-Orca regression checks.

The incidents that produced these rules are in [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md). Historical logs and spike procedures are in [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

10	
11	- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
12	- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
13	- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
14	- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.

21	## Logo use
22	
23	The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.
24	
25	- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
26	- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
27	- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
28	- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
29	- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.

32	Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

34	## Brand palette
35	
36	| Name | Value | Use |
37	|---|---:|---|
38	| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
39	| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
40	| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
41	| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
42	| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
43	| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
44	| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
45	| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
46	| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
47	| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |
48

52	
53	## Semantic color behavior
54	
55	Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.
56	
57	Core mappings include:
58	
59	| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
60	|---|---:|---:|---|
61	| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
62	| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
63	| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
64	| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
65	| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
66	| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
67	| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
68	| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
69	| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
70	| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |
71	
72	The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.
73	
74	## Typography
75	
76	Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:
77	
78	- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
79	- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
80	- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
81	- The system GUI font as fallback.
82	- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.
83	
84	HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
85	and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
86	not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.
87	
88	Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.
89	
90	| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
91	|---|---:|---|
92	| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
93	| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
94	| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
95	| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
96	| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
97	| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
98	| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
99	| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
100	| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
101	| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
102	| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |
103	
104	The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
105	action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
106	its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
107	text around it is.
108	
109	## Layout and geometry
110	
111	Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.
112	
113	- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
114	- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
115	- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
116	- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
117	- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
118	- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
119	  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
120	  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
121	  rather than a stripe across it.
122	- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.
123	
124	Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.
125	
126	## Components and states
127	
128	Use the existing native component density and established SVG icon library. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.
129	
130	- Functional icons: 16, 20, or 24 DIP, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it.
131	- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
132	- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
133	- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
134	- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
135	- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
136	- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
137	- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
138	- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
139	- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
140	- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
141	- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
142	- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.
143	
144	Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.
145	
146	## Accessibility
147	
148	- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
149	- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
150	- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
151	- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
152	- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
153	- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
154	- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.
155	
156	## Writing UI code
157	
158	Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
159	exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
160	the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
161	only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
162	
163	1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
164	   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
165	   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
166	   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
167	   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
168	   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
169	   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
170	   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
171	   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
172	2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
173	   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
174	   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
175	   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
176	   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
177	   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
178	   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
179	3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
180	   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
181	   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
182	4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
183	   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
184	   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
185	5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
186	   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
187	   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
188	   token file records what stayed.
189	6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
190	   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
191	   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
192	   not that the result looks right.
193	7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
194	   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
195	   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
196	   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.
197	
198	## Runtime application in the native app
199	
200	The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
201	three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
202	color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
203	three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.
204	
205	1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
206	   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
207	   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
208	     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
209	     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
210	     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
211	     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
212	     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
213	     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
214	     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
215	     fonts.
216	   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
217	     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
218	     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
219	     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
220	     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
221	     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
222	     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
223	   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
224	     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
225	     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
226	     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
227	     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
228	     translucent rounded rectangles.
229	2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
230	   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
231	   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
232	   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
233	   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
234	     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
235	     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
236	     switches at once.
237	   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
238	     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
239	     color.
240	   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
241	     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
242	     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
243	     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
244	     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
245	     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
246	     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
247	   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
248	     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
249	     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
250	   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
251	     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
252	   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
253	     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
254	     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
255	     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
256	3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
257	   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
258	     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
259	     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
260	     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
261	   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
262	     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
263	     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
264	     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
265	     in About are excluded by the script.
266	   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
267	     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
268	     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
269	     reference it.
270	
271	`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
272	contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
273	the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
274	`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
275	the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
276	12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
277	button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.
278	
279	Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
280	teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
281	Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
282	links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
283	generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
284	were not visually verified.
285	
286	## Design handoff requirements
287	
288	Every high-fidelity product frame must:
289	
290	1. Include paired light and dark versions using the same semantic token names.
291	2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
292	3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
293	4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
294	5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
295	6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
296	7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
297	8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.
298	
299	The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the original logo, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.

Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.

## Semantic color behavior

Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.

Core mappings include:

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|

| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |

| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |

- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.

  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
  rather than a stripe across it.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states
